html:
On 27 September 1996 the Taliban, a movement of religious students from the Pashtun south, took Kabul and declared the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan under Mullah Mohammad Omar.

The Taliban began in Kandahar in 1994, promising to end the chaos of the civil war, with support from Pakistan. In Kabul they publicly hanged the former communist president Najibullah. They banned girls' schooling and women's work, music and television, and enforced their rules with public punishments. Only three countries recognised them.

They gave shelter to Osama bin Laden and al-Qaeda. In March 2001 they blew up the Buddhas of Bamiyan, and that September Ahmad Shah Massoud, their main enemy, was assassinated, two days before the 11 September attacks. The American-led invasion then drove them from power.
sum: On 27 September 1996 the Taliban, a movement of religious students from the Pashtun south, took Kabul and declared the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan under Mullah Mohammad Omar.
